title: Zero-to-Pilot SDK demo: 5-day sprint plan
summary: A compact, execution-oriented 5-day sprint plan and playbook to take a Redwood SDK integration from zero to a customer-facing pilot demo. Focus: low-friction onboarding, deterministic telemetry, clear acceptance criteria, and fallback plans for common failure modes.
audience: SDK engineers, developer advocates, solutions engineers, product PMs
goals: Ship a reproducible sample app that exercises text generation + streaming in Redwood SDK
Capture and display token-level latency + cost telemetry in the demo UI
Create a 5-minute quickstart that an engineer can follow to run the demo locally
Produce a lightweight runbook for handoffs and a short retrospective template
success_metrics: Local demo run time < 10 minutes from checkout to first token
Telemetry visible in UI within 30s of first request
README quickstart under 300 words + 3 shell commands
Two customers or internal partners accept the pilot demo as satisfactory for next-stage evaluation
constraints: One small dev pool (2 GPU dev nodes) for live tests. No infra changes allowed beyond feature flags. Keep friction minimal — prefer config over code changes for demo variations.
day_by_day: Day 0 (prep): confirm dev pool access, create a repo scaffold with README template, stub telemetry endpoint, reserve a 60-min demo slot with stakeholders.

Day 1: Core plumbing - implement minimal SDK sample app (node + python presets), wire Redwood client calls, validate generation + streaming locally. QA checklist: request/response works, handles 5 concurrent clients.

Day 2: Telemetry & cost - add simple client-side instrumentation: token counters, per-request latency, and cost estimator. Send telemetry to a mock endpoint and visualize in a tiny web UI (chart + recent requests).

Day 3: Quickstart + packaging - simplify repo: 3 commands to run (install, env, start). Add env var examples, screenshots, and a single script to prefill prompts for demo. Runthrough with solutions engineer and iterate docs.

Day 4: Resilience & fallbacks - test network loss, token limit errors, and model unavailability. Add fallback policies: retry backoff, model-variant fallback, lightweight local stub for offline demo. Update runbook with troubleshooting steps.
Day 5: Demo rehearsal & retro - run a 20-minute rehearsal with target audience, collect feedback, ship final README and one-pager, run 15-minute retrospective and capture action items.
deliverables: Mini web UI showing last 20 requests with latency/cost sparklines
Runbook: demo checklist + rollback steps + quick debugging guide
Retrospective notes with prioritized action items (owner + ETA)
quickstart_outline:
1) git clone && cd examples/zero-to-pilot
2) cp .env.example .env and set REDWOOD_API_KEY
3) npm install (or pip install -r requirements.txt)
4) npm run start:demo (or python run_demo.py) -> open http://localhost:3000 to see streaming tokens and telemetry
troubleshooting_cheats: If no tokens stream: ensure API key env var set and network egress allowed. If telemetry missing: verify telemetry endpoint URL in .env and check dev console for failed POSTs. For high latencies: toggle small_model variant in .env to reduce sequence length and retry.
runbook_checklist: Pre-demo: confirm dev pool health and task queue drained
Pre-demo: set DEMO_MODE=true and small_model=true in demo env
Start: run demo start script and confirm UI reachable
During: monitor telemetry panel, note any rate limit warnings
Post-demo: collect logs, share retro notes, and mark action items
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: GPU dev pool throttled -> mitigation: switch to model-variant with CPU-friendly quantized profile
Risk: Interactive demo stalls on long generation -> mitigation: enforce max_tokens=150 and use streaming partials in UI
Risk: Telemetry endpoint overloaded -> mitigation: sample 1/10 requests in demo mode and batch sends
handoff_notes: Assign an on-call owner for the demo window. Provide the solutions engineer with a trimmed debug checklist and an emergency rollback command that switches the demo to a local stub. Share GitHub link and the single-line deploy/run commands in Slack channel #sdk-demos.
postmortem_template: Title, Date, Participants, What happened (timeline), Impact, Root cause, Actions (owner + ETA), Follow-ups
notes_to_self: Keep the quickstart mnemonic-friendly. Prioritize reproducibility over bells and whistles. If time is tight, cut the web UI and use a simple CLI logging view that prints token+latency lines.
future_extensions: Add an A/B variant in the repo to compare batching vs. no-batching cost
Integrate with Redwood Console traces for token-level attribution
Create a downloadable one-click demo package for enterprise trials
